requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to present each group to the user with its exact text, including any `{sites}` and `{violations}` queries, and with each design question the review returned, along with its options and the presenting agent's recommendation.
rationale:
structural: The requirement says the `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to present each group with its exact text (including any `{sites}` and `{violations}` queries) and with each design question, its options and the presenting agent's recommendation. Every clause is about what the skill document tells agents to do. None prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface.

I tried an alternative for each clause. A skill that words the same instruction differently, or puts it in another section, still satisfies the text. So how the instruction is built is discretionary, and no structural obligation needs an {impl} root.

The supplied root `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` does contain the instruction in `section[Habeas requirements]/section[Workflow]`, step 4. It reads: "Present each group to the user: its exact text, including any `{sites}` and `{violations}` queries, and the design questions the review returned, each with its options and your recommendation." That matches the requirement's wording, so no gap shows up.

behavioral: The requirement's only obligation is that the `habeas-requirements` skill directs agents to present each group to the user with three things. These are its exact text, including any `{sites}` and `{violations}` queries; each design question the review returned; and, for each question, its options and the agent's recommendation.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_presents_exact_text_and_design_questions]` covers this. It calls `assert_phrases("habeas-requirements", ...)`, which reads the bundled skill through `bundled_skill`. `bundled_skill` joins `SKILL.md` with the skill's reference files and collapses the whitespace. `assert_text` then asserts that the text contains the phrase. The phrase is "Present each group to the user: its exact text, including any `{sites}` and `{violations}` queries, and the design questions the review returned, each with its options and your recommendation".

The phrase has every element of the requirement: presenting to the user, each group, exact text, `{sites}` and `{violations}` queries, the design questions returned, and the options and recommendation for each question. The assertion fails with a message if the phrase is removed or reworded. Because the obligation is about the content of the skill text, this check tests it. No other behavioral obligation or boundary case needs a test.
